lines.note: Ienji (zenji), glossed Yoqi coto, denotes a good thing or virtuous deeds; the Portuguese introduces the moral sense developed in the examples.
Ienjiuo voconǒ means to perform good deeds. The Japanese example is roman and the introductory Vt and Portuguese translation are italic.
Restored the visible paragraph sign before Ienji jengon, the pairing of good deeds and good words; Idem refers back to the virtuous conduct just described.
The homophonous Ienji (zenji) is a master of the Zen teaching, not the preceding word for good deeds; Ienxùs occurs inside the Portuguese explanation.
Restored the headword’s capital I. Ienjit and xenjit are alternative readings for the preceding day, explained by Mayeno fi; l introduces the alternative form.
The continuation broadens the preceding-day gloss to days in the past. It belongs to Ienjit, rather than opening a new entry.
Ienjǒ (zenjō), explained by Mayeno vmare, means a former birth or existence; the Portuguese description continues on the next row.

Corrected cote to core in the example, “all this [is] of a former existence.” Retained poſſada: its first vowel has the round, worn form reflected by the baseline, although passada is the expected Portuguese word.

Ingua nari completes the claim that everything is the karmic consequence of a former existence. The Portuguese has the joined form empago and ends with retri-, continued by the omitted row restored below.

runs.text: buição do que fez noutra idade, ou nacimento.

lines.note: Restored this entire physical row from the scan. Together with retri- it reads retribution for what one did in another age or birth, completing the karmic explanation of the Japanese example.
Ienmai (zenmai) names an edible fern; the Portuguese merely calls it an herb so named, without supplying a more specific botanical description.
Corrected Ierano to Ienno and reunited virtude. Ienno agiuai is the taste or savor of virtue, explaining Ienmi rather than a separate example.
Ienmǒ, explained by Ienno nozomi, denotes good wishes or a desire for virtue. The visible text ends deſe without a secure terminal hyphen; it continues with jo on the next row.
Jo completes deſejo from the preceding row, without a printed hyphen at that break. The whole Ienmi definition concerns taking pleasure in, or desiring, virtue.
Restored the capital I of Ienmon. Camiuo ſotta fito describes a person with the hair shaved, matching the Portuguese phrase split across this and the following row.

runs.text: do. ¶ Item, Bonzo da ſeita dos Ienxùs.

lines.note: Completes rapado and adds the more specific sense of a monk of the Ienxùs sect. The worn internal letters of Bonzo are retained as the recognizable printed word.
Iennanxi (zennan-shi) denotes a virtuous man; this short, complete entry has no continuation on the next row.
Iennaua is referred to Ieninaua, the cord used for threading cash coins on the preceding page; the damaged medial letters do not warrant a different cross-reference.
Corrected the final OCR a in penſamentoa to s. Yoqi nen means good thoughts, distinguishing this entry from the chronological Iennen immediately below.
Iennen and xennen, explained by Mayeno toxi, denote previous years. The Portuguese plural Annos continues with its adjective on the following row.
The short continuation supplies “past” for the preceding Annos. Retained the baseline’s paſados rather than regularizing the historical spelling.
Iennhonin is explained by Yoqi vonna, a good woman; the Portuguese calls her virtuous and continues with an alternative characterization on the next row.
The alternative “or holy” completes the description of the virtuous woman. Preserved the historical spelling ſancta.
Restored Ienni’s capital I, mistaken for long ſ in OCR. Bicuni identifies a Buddhist nun, described as a shaven woman or nun in the Portuguese.
Iapão completes “nun of Japan”; it is a Portuguese place-name here, not another Japanese headword.
Restored Iennin’s initial I and corrected the damaged OCR readings Hemem vintueſo to Homem virtuoſo. Yoqi fito means a good person, matching the Portuguese definition.
The continuation adds “holy” as an alternative description of the good person. It closes Iennin before the entry concerning predecessors.
Restored the capital I of Ienpai. Mayeno tomogara points to predecessors, while the Portuguese describes a man of an earlier time; antiguo is retained as printed.
The continuation describes someone from past times. Joined paſa do: the apparent gap is damaged letterwork within the word, not a meaningful word division; retained the single long ſ of the baseline.
Ienpen is glossed Mayeno fen, the preceding part. The Portuguese first describes a complete volume containing multiple books or parts, with that description continuing below.

runs.text: de muitos liuros, ou partes. ¶ Item, Ali

lines.note: Completes the description of a volume made up of several books or parts; Item then opens another usage. Ali belongs with quando on the following row and has no secure terminal hyphen.

runs.text: quando, Paragrapho, ou capitulo paſſado, ou

lines.note: Joined Paragra pho to the printed word Paragrapho. With Ali above, Aliquando introduces the occasional sense of a preceding paragraph or chapter, consistent with Mayeno fen.
“Or which lies behind” completes the preceding-paragraph sense of Ienpen. The row is a continuation, not a new entry.
Ienpit, glossed Ienno fude, refers to a particular manner of writing; the explanation of its letter forms continues over the next two rows.

runs.text: caracteres que os Bonzos Ienxùs folgão de imi-

lines.note: Corrected Iemxus to the visible Ienxùs. These are the character forms that Zen monks take pleasure in imitating; imi- continues into tar below.

runs.text: tar à ſemelhança das letras da China.

lines.note: Completes imitar and specifies imitation of Chinese letter forms. The comparison belongs to the calligraphic definition, not to an additional headword.
Ienpô is explained by Yoqi nori, a good law or teaching; the Portuguese gives the compact equivalent Boa ley.
Corrected Iamilia to Familia: the worn initial retains the form of F. Ienno iye is a Zen house or lineage, described as a family or order in Portuguese.
Corrected the OCR initial t to I. The word completes “family or order of the Ienxùs,” so it is an embedded Japanese sect-name, not a separate entry.
Ienqiô, explained by Yoqi voxiye, denotes good teaching or doctrine. The circumflex in the supplied headword is retained rather than normalized to a modern reading.
Removed the spurious a in Ienaqi and restored the whole example opening Ien- to roman type. This Ienqi denotes horsemen who go ahead, distinguished from the homophonous Zen term below.

The example says that before the leading riders have gone, riders behind come close after them. Retained the visibly repeated qi in goqiqi rather than silently replacing it with the expected goqi; the Portuguese translation begins with Não.

runs.text: tendo ainda paſſado diante os de caualo, ja lhe

lines.note: Corrected ju to the visible ja. The translation describes the rear riders already close behind before those in front have passed; its sentence continues on the next row.

runs.text: hião nas coſtas os de de tras.

lines.note: The rear riders were following close on the leaders’ backs. Preserved hião and the separately written de tras as historical Portuguese forms.
Corrected the sect-name’s damaged vowel to Ienxùs and made the complete example fragment Iẽ- roman. This Ienqi is the substance or spirit of Zen, not the preceding word for riders.

runs.text: He homem que tem eſpirito dos

lines.note: Restored the dropped p in eſpirito. Iẽ-qi aru fito describes a person possessing the spirit of Zen; the Portuguese translation continues below.

runs.text: Ienxùs, ou penetra as ſuas couſas.

lines.note: Restored Ienxùs and the continuation indentation. The translation ends by saying that the person penetrates or understands the matters of the Ienxùs; this is not an independent headword.
Restored the partly lost initial I of Ienqua, the reward or fruit of virtue. Goxeni begins an example concerning the next life, continued below.
Voite jenquauo toru bexi completes the statement that one will receive virtue’s reward in the next life. The Portuguese translation begins here and continues after vi-.

runs.text: da recebereis o premio da virtude. S.

lines.note: Completes vida and the translation promising reward for virtue. Separated the terminal S. usage label from the italic Portuguese sentence.

runs.text: Lugar onde ha muitos Bonzos Ienxùs.

lines.note: Corrected tenxùs to Ienxùs. Ienrin describes a place with many Zen monks, corresponding to the institutional sense of a Zen monastic community.
Restored Ienrio’s capital I. The Portuguese identifies a companion or fellow member of the Ienxùs, whose sect-name is embedded in the definition.
Kept the whole Ienſa example opening in roman type, removing an isolated italic e. Ienno xoſa explains the entry as good actions or deeds.
Ienſa uo yamuru means to stop doing good deeds. The Portuguese Ceſsar de fazer boas obras translates this first example, not the following positive injunction.
The paragraph sign opens a contrasting example: Ienſauo tçutomuru, to apply oneself to good deeds. Its Portuguese explanation continues with virtude below.
Virtude completes “to do works of virtue,” closing the second Ienſa example before the separate asthma entry.
Ienſocu is asthma; Ayequ iqi describes panting breath. Retained the visible q in Ayequ rather than modernizing the spelling to reflect aegu.
Changed the OCR uppercase V to the printed lowercase v in vazzurǒ. With Ienſocu above, the expression means to suffer from asthma.

runs.text: Ienxùs, ou profeßores da ley dos Ienxùs.

lines.note: Ienſu denotes the Ienxùs, explained as adherents of their teaching; Portuguese profeßores here means professing followers, not necessarily modern academic professors.
Corrected Maitai to Mattai, the whole or complete body. The Portuguese definition explicitly includes its members, supplied in the following row.
Membros completes the definition of the entire body with its members. The stain beside the text does not represent additional letters.

runs.text: Pratica dos Ienxùs, ou pontos de medi

lines.note: Read the damaged opening as Pratica, with the surviving bowl of capital P, and restored Ienxùs and medi. Ienua concerns Zen discussion or practice, explained as points of meditation; medi continues into tação without a visible terminal hyphen.
Completes meditação and states that these are the matters the Ienxùs discuss or practice. The row remains part of the Ienua definition.
Ienxa is explained by Yoqi mono and the synonym Iennin, a good person. Iennin is a Japanese synonym, not an embedded term in the Portuguese gloss.
The phrase “or virtuous” completes the definition of a good person, separating this entry from the following homophone for a leading carriage.
Ienxa, glossed Saqino curuma, is the carriage ahead. The Portuguese word diante breaks at dian- and continues below.
The example begins by observing the overturning of the carriage in front. The roman Japanese phrase follows italic Vt and continues into the next row.
Côxano imaximeto naſu makes the leading carriage’s overturning a warning to those behind. Xix. is the roman source label; the Portuguese translation begins with O car-.

runs.text: ro que vai diante ſe cae, dà auiſo aos que vão

lines.note: The Portuguese explains that when the carriage ahead falls, it warns those following. Retained the grave accent in dà and the historical unaccented cae.

runs.text: aßi o exemplo dos que vão diante, &c.

lines.note: Corrected iras to tras. The proverb’s warning is generalized to the example set by those who go before; retained the colon and aßi.
Ienxei is explained by Yoqi matçurigoto, good government. The Portuguese begins “good laws and ordinances”; or continues into denaçoens below without a secure terminal hyphen.
Completes ordenaçoens and adds “or good government.” Retained the historical spelling of ordinances and gouerno.
The second Ienxei is explained by Mattacu ſacannari, flourishing fully. It is distinct from the preceding word for good government, despite the same printed headword.
Corrected jeuxeina to the visible jenxeina. The example says that the present age flourishes; Eſ begins its Portuguese translation and continues with ta below.
Completes Eſta and translates the example as “this age is flourishing and prosperous.” The original spelling florente is retained.
Read the visibly tall ſ in Meſtre. This Ienxi is a former or first teacher, distinguished from the following entry for a Zen master.
Restored the capital I in Ienxùs. The Portuguese describes a master of the Zen sect rather than a teacher from earlier times.
Restored the capital I of the synonym Ientai. Mattai mi specifies the whole body, connecting this entry with the earlier Ientai definition.
The alternative Ienxin or jenxinna describes a virtuous person. It is the moral homophone, not the preceding word for the whole body.
Completes the description as good-hearted and devout. The ampersand and deuoto are retained as printed.
Ienxit is explained by Ienno iye, a Zen house; the Portuguese places Ienxùs inside the definition, so the sect-name is eligible for whole-word typeface review.
Ienxo, glossed Yoqi tocoro, is a good place, described in religious terms as a place of salvation. The explanatory i, remains inside the Portuguese passage.

runs.text: Lugar onde ſe exercita a virtude, & procura

lines.note: The place is one where virtue is practiced and salvation sought. Procura takes its object from the following row; no text is missing at this line break.
Corrected Coxǒ to Goxǒ: the capital G has a visible inner stroke. Goxǒ jenxo concerns a good destination in the next life, glossed as Paradise on the following row.
Paraiſo supplies the entire Portuguese gloss of Goxǒ jenxo. It is a short continuation, not another Japanese entry.
Ienxǒ taixi is given as the name of Amida when a child. Preserved minino and the printed accents; Amida is embedded in the Portuguese explanation.
Restored Ienxǔ’s initial I in place of the OCR F. The caron-marked headword denotes people of the Zen sect, and the definition contains the separate form Ienxùs.
Restored the initial I of Ienxu, good seed, explained by Yoqi tane. The example opening Ien- continues on the next row.
Ien-xuuo vyuru means to sow good seed. Corrected the punctuation after the explanatory i to the visible comma; Boas introduces the moral interpretation continued below.

runs.text: obras pera depois colher fruito na outra vida.

lines.note: The seeds are good works performed now to reap fruit in another life. This is the explanatory extension of the agricultural metaphor, not a new entry.
Another Ienxu is explained by Ienno xuguiǒ, the practice or exercise of virtue. Retained the lack of a secure terminal full stop rather than supplying one editorially.
Restored Ienxùs from the OCR tenxùs. Ienno coromo identifies the clothing or habit worn by the Zen sect.
Ienyen is affinity or alliance with virtue. The Portuguese liança is retained without inserting a modern initial a; its example follows below.

Restored Ienyenni’s initial I and read ſomu rather than ſomiu. The alternatives describe becoming attached or drawn to virtue; Afeiço- continues on the next page, anticipated by the separate arſe catchword.
